So funny story. I've been playing the dos version of WIzardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord recently.

That game is fucking bullshit. Absolute, insane, ridiculous bullshit.

It's just arbitrarily stupidly hard for no reason. 30 seconds into my last session, the moment I got down to level 3 of the dungeon, my entire party was ambushed by about 30 ninjas (4 groups of 5-7 each) and every single party member got decapitated in the surprise attack. No chance for me to do anything.

Ok, fine, I recover them, spend all my money trying to revive them, and every single revive at the Temple of Cant fails turns them to ash and I'm out of money. And my only recourse is to start over. There is no savegame. You are playing in constant ironman mode. No backsies.

Which is absolute bullshit when the game will just arbitrarily kill everyone and wipe out all your progress at a moments notice. You don't have ironman mode, permadeath, and enemies on every floor that have an insta-kill special ability. You are given zero tools to mitigate this risk. Nothing. Just pray it doesn't happen to you.

To make matters worse, there is a zero risk power levelling room on the first floor. The monsters have a lot of life and are hard to hit, but only do 2 damage per hit and have no special abilities. They are worth about 750 XP each. You frequently encounter 2 at a time, for 1500 xp an encounter. The enemies on the 3rd floor where instant arbitrary death lurks behind every door? I typically get between 1000-2000 xp.

So basically the game is telling me to stay on the 1st floor and power level until....?

I was so pissed off I just hex edited all my characters back to life. I figure if the game is gonna cheat like that, so will I. Although I'm considering that my one get out of jail free, and now I make a backup of the dsk file every time I start the game.

With that rant out of the way, it's really fascinating to me seeing the traces of modern games in WIzardry. I'm pretty sure it invented graphical dungeons you needed to map out, with puzzles. I'm pretty sure it also pioneered having a group of characters instead of just 1 in an RPG, as well as a rudimentary job system like you see in a lot of JRPGs. Playing it has been really fascinating.
